classification.tone: gritty, pulpy, heightened, mean-spirited, darkly comic

evaluation.positioning_hook: A group of arrogant snowboarders gets trapped at a remote ski lodge, where an ancient skin-stealing curse turns their mountain getaway into a brutal survival nightmare.

audience_appeal_marketability.reasoning: The premise is instantly legible to horror audiences: isolated lodge, storm, missing friends, escalating body horror. The snowboarder milieu gives it a youth-skewing, high-energy entry point, and the cat-and-mouse survival structure is easy to sell in a single sentence.

conceptual_hook_clarity.reasoning: The hook lands early through the old Indian’s story and the move to the lodge, then pays off with Patamon’s transformation and the skin-collecting curse. The rules are simple enough to track: stay in the wrong place, get hunted, and the curse is tied to skin and nature.

character_appeal_and_long_term_potential.reasoning: The characters are sharply differentiated by attitude and function—Brandon’s swagger, Trent’s decency, Desmond’s awkward sensitivity, Jennifer’s intelligence, Greg’s vanity—but they mostly operate as archetypes in a pressure cooker. Trent and Brandon carry the strongest dramatic friction, and Desmond has the most memorable specificity.

creative_originality_and_boldness.reasoning: The script commits hard to a lurid, old-school exploitation mode, with a Native folklore framing device, a ski-lodge setting, and transformation imagery built around stolen skins. The boldness is in the unapologetic pulp and the visual extremity, even when the underlying engine is familiar.

narrative_momentum_engagement.reasoning: The setup is efficient, the lodge arrival is clean, and the disappearances escalate the tension in a steady line. The back half becomes a chase-and-reveal machine with strong set-piece energy, though the story is more about attrition than surprise.

resonant_originality.reasoning: The central idea is memorable—a skin-collecting mountain curse targeting snowboarders—but it plays in a recognizable slasher grammar. What makes it stick is the specific iconography of the lodge, the lift, the storm, and the pelt transformation ritual.

world_density_and_texture.reasoning: The mountain lodge, ski lift, backcountry terrain, and snowboard culture give the script a usable world with clear physical geography. The old Indian’s story adds mythic texture, and the lift system becomes part of the danger architecture.

tonal_specificity.reasoning: This has a very specific grindhouse tone: juvenile banter, profanity, stoner comedy, then sudden, graphic mutilation. The tonal identity is hard-edged and unapologetic, with the old-world curse story giving it a campfire-horror flavor.

latent_depth_slow_burn_potential.reasoning: The script is built to deliver immediate genre gratification rather than layered subtext. There are hints of identity and inheritance in Trent’s polio backstory and the brother dynamic, but the dominant pleasure is the surface-level survival horror engine.

relationship_density_and_ensemble_engine.reasoning: The ensemble has clear internal tensions—Trent/Brandon, Trent/Desmond, Greg/Jennifer—but the story ultimately narrows to a few survival pairings. The group banter gives the opening a social charge, and the breakdown of that group is the engine.

casting_characteristics: Male ensemble in late teens to early 20s
One older Native man with folkloric authority
Physical performance required for monster transformation

notable_requirements: Snow-covered forest and ski lift infrastructure
Practical cabin interiors with basement and operator booth

technical.vfx_details: Creature transformation, skinned bodies, blood effects, storm enhancement, and a few stylized visual beats like the face in the windshield and lightning-driven reveals.
technical.sfx_needs: Heavy practical blood and gore, skinned corpse effects, prosthetic creature makeup, and cat injury effects.

rights_flags.detail: Specific snowboarding publication referenced in the final letter to the editor

platform_fit.recommended_lane: theatrical genre feature / streaming horror lane
platform_fit.series_engine_or_release_model: Feature release model: festival-to-platform, genre theatrical, or direct-to-streaming horror audience

cost.note: Contained lodge-and-forest setting keeps the footprint manageable, but creature work, gore effects, snow work, and night exteriors push it above microbudget.

cast.note: The cast is small and youth-skewing, with no star-dependent roles or large ensemble logistics beyond the core group.

location.note: A remote mountain setting, ski lift infrastructure, snow conditions, and storm sequences create some logistical lift, though the geography is still contained.

content.note: Graphic skinning, dismemberment, nudity, profanity, and prolonged gore place it firmly in mature horror territory.

rights.note: The script is mostly original; the only notable clearance items are a brand card and a named publication reference.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The ski-lodge setting is a clean horror engine.
strengths.what_it_means: The mountain, lift, storm, and isolated cabin create a naturally producible pressure cooker with built-in geography for suspense. It’s the kind of contained world that gives a producer a clear budget lane and gives the audience a simple, playable fear map.
strengths.evidence: The lodge, lift station, forest trail, and backcountry terrain all become active parts of the danger, especially once the storm cuts them off.

strengths.dimension_or_area: Patamon is a memorable monster concept.
strengths.what_it_means: The curse is not just a killer; it has a ritual logic built around stolen skin, which gives the movie a signature visual identity. That kind of body-horror mythology is exactly what genre buyers remember and market.
strengths.evidence: The old Indian’s story culminates in Patamon’s transformation and later reveals him as a seven-foot flesh-and-bone predator made of other people’s skins.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The opening group dynamic is instantly readable.
strengths.what_it_means: The script gives each rider a distinct social function fast: the alpha, the skeptic, the nerd, the girlfriend, the stoner couple. That makes the early pages easy to follow and gives the eventual body count emotional shape.
strengths.evidence: The SUV banter, the cat carrier, the fashion jokes, and the store stop establish the group’s hierarchy and friction in a few pages.

strengths.dimension_or_area: Desmond is the standout character texture.
strengths.what_it_means: He’s the kind of oddball supporting role actors like to play: intelligent, anxious, tender, and socially out of step. His relationship to the cat gives the script a humanizing thread that makes the carnage land harder.
strengths.evidence: His book on Native tribes, his protective behavior toward Neebes, and his discomfort around the others make him feel specific immediately.

strengths.what_it_means: Each disappearance is staged as a distinct horror beat rather than a repeat of the last, which keeps the movie moving and gives the producer a clear trailer path. The lift, the storm, the basement, and the final cave sequence all feel like event moments.
strengths.evidence: Greg’s attack in the woods, Desmond’s skinned cat reveal, Paul’s brutal lift-area death, and Trent’s final transformation each escalate the threat in a new way.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The tone has old-school grindhouse confidence.
strengths.what_it_means: This knows exactly what kind of movie it is: profane, lurid, funny, and vicious. That clarity is valuable because it makes the project easy to position for genre fans who want a hard R, no-apologies experience.
strengths.evidence: The dialogue is packed with insults and jokes, then the script pivots into graphic mutilation and transformation without softening the blow.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The old Indian story gives the movie a campfire frame.
strengths.what_it_means: The folklore sequence creates a mythic spine and a built-in exposition device that feels like part of the entertainment rather than a lecture. It also gives the movie a clear “legend becomes real” hook.
strengths.evidence: The store scene where he tells the Patamon tale directly precedes the group’s descent into the mountain.

whats_special.headline: PELTS is a lean, nasty mountain horror piece with a strong contained setting, a memorable skin-stealing monster, and a youth-cast ensemble that gives the carnage a social charge. It’s built for genre buyers who want a clear hook, practical production footprint, and a hard-R payoff with a distinct visual signature.

lead_characters.name: Trent Harty
lead_characters.hook: Trent is the emotional center of the movie: the quieter, more grounded brother who gets forced into leadership when the macho posturing collapses. He has a protective streak, a skeptical intelligence, and a buried vulnerability that the script sharpens with his history of childhood polio. He’s not the loudest guy in the room, but he becomes the one with the most moral weight.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is a survival-horror lead with a real arc: from sidelined brother to the last man standing. It gives an actor a chance to play fear, decency, physical endurance, and final resolve in a role that sits in the same performance lane as the straight-man heroism of a young Kevin Bacon in Tremors or the grounded panic-to-action turn in The Descent.

lead_characters.name: Brandon Duncan
lead_characters.hook: Brandon is the swaggering alpha who talks first, drives too fast, and mistakes volume for authority. He’s funny, abrasive, selfish, and weirdly magnetic, which makes him useful as both comic engine and pressure-point antagonist inside the group. He’s the kind of character who can dominate a room and still reveal panic the second the mountain turns on him.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is a juicy, scene-stealing part for an actor who can weaponize charm and then let it curdle. The role has the same kind of volatile, cocky energy that makes supporting turns memorable in horror and crime films, with room for a performer to play arrogance, humiliation, and survival instinct in quick succession.

lead_characters.name: Desmond Harty
lead_characters.hook: Desmond is the outsider with the cat carrier, the tribal history book, and the social awkwardness that makes him both comic and touching. He’s observant, anxious, and deeply attached to Neebes, which gives him a tenderness the rest of the group lacks. He feels like the one person in the van who is actually paying attention to the world around him.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is a character actor gift: eccentric, vulnerable, and instantly identifiable. It gives a performer a chance to play innocence under siege, with the kind of offbeat specificity that can become a cult favorite in the way memorable horror side characters do in films like The Burbs or Shaun of the Dead.

lead_characters.name: Jennifer Martin
lead_characters.hook: Jennifer is the smartest person in the group and one of the few who sees the danger before it’s too late. She’s sharp, sexually frank, and not interested in pretending the boys are more competent than they are. That combination of intelligence and impatience gives her a strong, modern presence inside a very old-school horror setup.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: The role lets an actor play wit, disgust, fear, and emotional collapse without losing authority. It’s the kind of part that can anchor a genre film with real personality, in the lane of strong horror survivors who are allowed to be funny, sexual, and skeptical before the terror takes over.

lead_characters.name: Patamon
lead_characters.hook: Patamon is the curse made flesh: a towering, diseased, skin-stitched predator whose body is a grotesque archive of his victims. He’s not just a slasher; he’s a mythic punishment figure with ritual logic, which makes him feel bigger than a standard masked killer. The design invites a full physical performance under heavy makeup and prosthetics.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: For a performer with creature-work chops, this is a showcase role in the tradition of iconic practical monsters. It offers physicality, menace, and transformation, with the kind of screen presence that can become the movie’s signature image.

director_appeal.hook: A director who loves practical horror, snowbound suspense, and grotesque creature imagery.
director_appeal.detail: This material rewards someone who can stage geography clearly and make every exterior feel hostile. The movie gives a director a chance to build dread out of weather, isolation, and physical space, then pay it off with big, memorable gore and a monster reveal that can sell the whole film.

buyer_appeal.lane: hard-R horror / cult genre / streaming horror
buyer_appeal.detail: This is sized for a contained horror buy: limited cast, one primary location cluster, and a monster concept that can be delivered with practical effects and selective VFX. It fits buyers looking for a clear poster image, a simple logline, and a reliable genre audience rather than four-quadrant scale.

considerations.area: The opening leans into broad teen banter.
considerations.detail: The early pages establish the group quickly, and a future pass could sharpen a few voices so each rider lands with even more distinction. The core dynamic is already clear; the opportunity is to make the banter feel even more character-specific and less interchangeable.

considerations.area: The folklore frame carries real sensitivity demands.
considerations.detail: Because the story uses Native identity and a tribal legend as the engine for the curse, the material benefits from careful cultural consultation and a clear production approach to representation. That attention would protect the movie and strengthen its credibility with audiences.

considerations.area: The final act is built for practical gore and creature execution.
considerations.detail: The pelt transformations, skinned bodies, and Patamon reveal are the movie’s selling images, so the production plan should foreground how those effects will be achieved. A strong effects strategy will make the film feel bigger than its budget.

considerations.area: This plays cleanly in the hard-R horror lane.
considerations.detail: The script’s profanity, nudity, and graphic mutilation point squarely at mature genre audiences, which is useful for positioning but narrows the buyer pool to the right lane. That clarity is an asset when packaging and marketing.

considerations.area: The mountain geography should stay legible.
considerations.detail: The lodge, lift, forest, and cave all work best when the audience can always understand where the characters are relative to the threat. Protecting that spatial clarity will keep the suspense clean and the chase sequences easy to follow.
